[center][b][size=5]Description[/size][/b][/center]
[center]This mod contains HD portrait replacements for Caroline.[/center]
[center]-[/center]
[b][color=#ff0000]Tired of AI-generated portraits?[/color][/b] Or maybe you want [b][color=#ff00ff]something different from pixel-art, anime-style, or hand-drawn[/color][/b] portraits? I give you these [b][color=#00ff00]handmade, 3D rendered[/color][/b] portraits, after weeks in the making and after many iterations to nail the final look and quality.

I used Virt-a-Mate (18+ NSFW software) as my base of operations for the model, posing, lighting, and rendering, and then edited the screenshots in post to patch up any rendering/modelling issues. The character model, as well as all the plugins used, are all under the [color=#00ff00]CC-BY/FC[/color] licenses which allow for editing and using them in free works such as this. There were too many assets to name so I'd like to thank the developers of VaM and the creators of all the assets used. I could only use what was [color=#00ff00]free-to-use[/color] so my options were somewhat limited (especially in the clothing department).

This is [b]my personal interpretation of Caroline[/b], and how I imagine she may look and dress when aiming for a realistic style. I tried to make her look as close to her original design as possible, but I did take some creative liberties either out of limitations or because I felt like it matched the character better. Apologies if you feel like her design is too far removed from what you imagined, but this is what I wanted to make.



[center][b][size=5]Main features[/size][/b][/center]
This mod contains 2 separate packs: [b]Bodyshots [/b]and [b]Headshots[/b]. Mix and match, run them in parallel, enable/disable in the GMCM. This is using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/41608?tab=description]JP's Shin HD Portraits Framework[/url] which seems to be the only HD Portrait framework that supports what I want to achieve.



[center][b][color=#00ff00][size=5]Pack Contents[/size][/color][/b][/center]
[b][color=#00ffff](Mod File 1) Bodyshots Pack:[/color] [/b]are larger in size (2048x2048 per expression) and are intended for full-screen usage (and at the full-zoom setting using the framework).

[b][color=#00ffff](Mod File 2) Headshots Pack:[/color][/b] are smaller (1024x1024 per expression) and are more in-line with how the vanilla portraits appear.

[b][color=#1e84cc]Pack Differences:[/color][/b] [color=#b6b6b6]Both packs are identical except for their bodyshot/headshot-focus, camera angles, and their sizes (resolution and file size).[/color]

[b][color=#00ffff]Included Portrait Sets:[/color][/b]
[list]
[*][b][color=#ff00ff]Seasonal Indoor and Outdoor portraits[/color][/b] (yes, [b]both Indoor AND Outdoor for EACH season[/b]) The overall outfit between seasons varies quite significantly. The Indoor versions offer different poses to the Outdoor versions. The outfit of the Indoor version is typically a more dressed-down take on the Outdoor version. These base ones are relatively [color=#00ff00]mild in their sexuality[/color].[/*]
[*][b][color=#ff00ff]Beach[/color][/b] A portrait mod wouldn't be complete without a beach variant for Ginger Island. This set is [color=#ffff00]moderately sexual[/color].[/*]
[*][b][color=#ff00ff]Festival-specific portraits[/color][/b] Currently only offering portraits for [b]Egg Festival[/b], [b]Spirits Eve[/b], and [b]Winter Star[/b]. These offer unique portraits that only appear for those specific festivals, where the NPC dresses up uniquely just for those events (and sometimes featuring props in the portraits). This mod also allows you to enable the festival-specific portraits for either the festival event itself [b]OR[/b] for the entire date of the festival (allowing you to see more of the expressions available compared to the limited NPC interaction present during the festival itself). These are a [color=#ff7700]lot more sexualised[/color] than the ones above.[/*]
[*][b][color=#ff00ff]Birthday Surprise[/color][/b] During the NPC's birthday they will have a [color=#ff0000]highly-sexualised (and slightly pornographic)[/color] set just for that date... enjoy![/*]
[/list]So that's 4 Outdoor Seasonal, 4 Indoor Seasonal, 1 Beach, 3 Festival-Specific, and 1 Birthday Suprise. That's 13 portrait sheets for each pack, making for a total of [b]26 portrait sheets[/b] in this entire mod!

[b][color=#980000]What this mod doesn't contain:[/color] [/b][color=#b6b6b6]There are [b]no[/b] new events, NPC sprites, or animations in this mod. It's purely just the portraits.[/color]



[center][b][size=5]Installation instructions[/size][/b][/center]
1. Install the required mods
2. Install either one or both of the file packs from this mod ([b]Bodyshots[/b] and/or [b]Headshots[/b]), depending on your preference
3. Open the GMCM (or respective config.json files) and set your mod settings accordingly; here you can enable/disable each individual mod pack, as well as set the "Festival Portraits All-Day" setting (true by default) to either display the Festival-Specific portrait sets on the entire day of that festival (true), or just for the festival event itself (false)
4. Follow the usage instructions on [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/41608?tab=description]JP's Shin HD Portraits Framework[/url] to cycle between different portrait mods and adjust your settings

[center][b][color=#ff0000][size=5]Known Issue(s)[/size][/color][/b][/center]
The HD Portrait framework that this mod uses had some bugs during development, but as of v1.0.6 of the framework, the bugs I was aware of have been fixed.

I've also noticed that enabling/disabling some of the settings in GMCM during gameplay doesn't always persist after saving and closing your new settings, and sometimes requires you to re-set your settings multiple times. I think this is either an issue with GMCM, the portrait framework, or Content Patcher, and there's seemingly nothing I can do about it.

Some portraits may have hints of coloured highlights, or the transparent edges of some clothes may be coloured. I used a greenscreen behind the models when taking the screenshots and as a result some environmental lighting or transparency issues have persisted. I've done what I can in post to remedy these issues, but until I can take screenshots with a transparent background in Virt-a-Mate itself, this issue will likely persist.

Some clothing materials can be affected by the compression settings of the screenshot plugin I was using, so the shading of some materials may show some banding; if I can find a way around this, I'll re-take the screenshots of any affected portraits.


[center][b][size=5]Bug/Feedback Reporting[/size][/b][/center]
First check the [b][color=#ff0000]Known Issues[/color][/b] above to make sure that you aren't reporting something already known about (as well as any bugs listed on the 'Bugs' section of this mod). I did not make the HD Portrait framework so I cannot help with issues regarding the framework itself.

[b][color=#ffff00]These are the only types of bugs you can report on this mod:[/color][/b]

1. Something wrong/strange about the portrait/expression itself. This is something you can spot in the files of this portrait mod itself, outside of running the game. Maybe some clothes, limbs, or objects are clipping strangely in the portrait image. Perhaps there's something "off" you find about the facial expression. Or maybe some of the images aren't correctly displaying in the portrait display box. Let me know and I'll see if I can improve it; there are some technical limitations with the software used to make the portraits so not everything is fixable, but I'll always listen to any feedback and do what I can to fix things.

2. A portrait should be appearing in a specific situation but isn't. This could be a bug with the framework, GMCM, or Content Patcher, but it could also be a bug with my content.json files. If you feel like a particular portrait set should be displaying within a certain situation, but isn't, then let me know. Make sure you double-check your config settings before reporting anything.

3. File contents not matching what is described in the mod.


[center][b][size=5]Requirements[/size][/b][/center]
Just install the required mods. Both of the packs provided by this mod are somewhat large in filesize; the Bodyshots pack is especially large in filesize. You [i]might [/i]need some decent RAM to get this mod running well, but I'm sure most players shouldn't hit any limitations.

[center][b][size=5]Compatibility[/size][/b]
[/center]
[left]This mod overwrites the NPC's portraits using an HD Portrait Framework. Other mods that use their own portraits may get priority over this one, especially if they're also Content Patch mods. Portrait mods always seem to conflict for SV, so I would suggest disabling any others that you have running if possible (although, this HD Portrait Framework that I'm using does allow cycling between other portrait mods, and now apparently also supports Portraiture mods since its version 1.1.0).

In case you're wondering if I'll support a specific mod one day (e.g. Valley Girls), it's unlikely without a modified version of that mod that uses the same HD Portrait Framework that I'm using. I'm not an expert with SV modding, but I think it could be possible one day, and likely only with the permission of other mod creators. If you're interested in seeing your favourite mods supported, make sure to let me know and maybe contact those mod creators to see if they can implement support for the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/41608?tab=description]HD Portrait Framework[/url] that I'm using.[/left]
